A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same diffusion-policy research, with substantial matched material. Their main text, Appendices A–C, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support comparison despite the expanded framework and changed layout.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture sampling experiments, MuJoCo returns, computational measurements, and diffusion-hyperparameter sensitivity results.

after.justification: v3 reports original sampling and MuJoCo experiments, including separate DPMD and SDAC results and an additional two-moon sampling comparison in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: v3 retains the reverse-sampling SDAC objective but adds DPMD, targeting a policy proportional to the previous policy times exp(Q/lambda), using current-policy samples followed by forward corruption. It also replaces v1's SDAC Q-standardization procedure with multiple reverse samples and logsumexp-normalized weights in Section 4.2 and Algorithm 2.

E1.justification: The ten MuJoCo v4 environments and Gaussian-mixture sampling task remain. Appendix C.4 adds a two-moon Boltzmann-sampling target with curved, separated modes, providing a limited extension of synthetic distribution coverage.

E2.justification: The MuJoCo comparator set remains PPO, TD3, SAC, QSM, DIPO, DACER, QVPO, and DPPO. The new two-moon comparison evaluates iDEM and FAB alongside RSM and DDPM; these additional samplers were not evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: The retained MuJoCo budgets, evaluation schedule, and hyperparameters in Tables 3–4 are unchanged. The added two-moon experiment introduces a documented model-size setting: Figure 5 labels FAB as using 20 times as many parameters as RSM.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 adds a qualitative sensitivity comparison of SDAC sampling distributions: uniform, current-policy, and noise-perturbed current-policy sampling reportedly perform similarly. The existing Ant diffusion-step and noise-schedule plots are retained, although v3 attributes them to DPMD rather than SDAC.

E5.justification: Both versions report MuJoCo means and standard deviations over five random seeds, with the same uncertainty convention for learning curves. v3 adds no new confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 reproduces every v1 SDAC score under DPMD and adds a separate SDAC row, including Ant 1391±202 and Swimmer 119.1±41.9. These are revised method-attributed results, not established same-method gains. Table 2 adds DPMD costs of 1192 MB and 21.10 minutes, and Figure 5 adds two-moon sampling results.

T1.justification: v3 generalizes the reweighting construction already present in v1's Appendix B.2 into an explicit positive-weight loss family. It adds the KL-proximal policy formulation and a derivation of the DPMD loss in Sections 2.1 and 4.1.1 and Appendix B.2.1, while revising the retained SDAC derivation.

C1.justification: The central contribution expands from RSSM and one maximum-entropy algorithm, SDAC, to a general RSM framework supporting both policy mirror descent and maximum-entropy optimization. The abstract's claim of over 120% improvement over SAC on Humanoid and Ant is now attributed to DPMD rather than SDAC.

C2.justification: v1 describes SDAC as consistently robust; v3 assigns that interpretation to DPMD and acknowledges SDAC's poor Ant performance. It newly explains SDAC's speed advantage through avoiding current-policy sampling and attributes FAB's connected two-moon samples to restrictions from invertible mappings.

D1.justification: v3 supplies an implementation repository link where v1 promised release upon acceptance. It also documents the additive-Gaussian approximation to policy log likelihood and explicit policy-evaluation formulas. The existing hardware specifications, network sizes, learning rates, and hyperparameter tables remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: The positioning expands substantially from maximum-entropy diffusion policies to proximity-based policy optimization and Boltzmann sampling. New discussions cite policy mirror-descent and trust-region literature, foundational score-matching work, and iDEM/FAB; DIME is also newly cited. The related-work appendix itself remains largely matched.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and core methodological narrative are extensively rewritten around RSM and two algorithms. v3 adds a separate energy-based-model primer, reorganizes Sections 3–4, moves SDAC pseudocode into Appendix C.2, and drops the SDAC prefix from the title.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column proceedings layout for the main text, replaces Figure 1's actor-critic pipeline with a score-reweighting illustration, expands Tables 1–2 and Figure 3 for two proposed algorithms, and adds Figure 5. Existing figures and tables are also resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The expanded derivations, additional sampler comparison, and implementation disclosures provide useful gains. However, Table 1 transfers v1's complete SDAC result row to DPMD without explaining the reassignment between differently defined methods. Section 5.2.2 also changes Walker2d gains to 41.7% and 43.4%, although Table 1 still implies approximately 35.0% over SAC and 36.7% over DACER. These central evidence and reporting ambiguities prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
